item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
Answers:

  • I don't think I said they 'feed' on vanity. SCP-XXXX-1 may use their castors vanity in their judgements/insults but not always. SCP-XXXX-1 will use anything to insults their castors. Also, all of this stems from the one important element. Reflections aren't naturally meant to reflect their castors. SCP-XXXX is the reason reflections act like reflections. Her maintaining her gaze in a way 'imprisons' reflections, forcing them to copy their castors actions every minute of every day. Think about how maddening that is. When SCP-XXXX-1 occurs, the reflections are going to use every possible second of freedom to emphasise how sickening it is being trapped. They don't just want to insult them. They want to degrade them. To put it simply, reflections are enslaved by their castors and the castors only discover this when SCP-XXXX-1 occurs. Then think about how the castors feel when they learn this. They've basically learnt that every reflection they cast is someone looking back at them, judging and hating them.
  • Also If you recall, I mentioned SCP-XXXX has a reflective coating on her inner eyelids. Whoever had her before the Foundation managed to coat her eyelids with this material. This is how she is able to blink and sleep. Now, one of the clinchers I have planned is to do with the decaying process. Her eyelid coatings are also decaying. Slowly but still at a noticeable rate. And unfortunately, the Foundation doesn't know how to replicate the material used to make it. Meaning, a day will come when her eyelid coating doesn't work anymore. Now the Foundations has a real problem!
  • Her mutilations are tied to why she doesn't age. Remember, she doesn't cause SCP-XXXX-1 but stops it from happening. Meaning, if she dies, SCP-XXXX-1 is permanent. So to prevent this from happening, her previous captors did something to make her immortal. They also gave her her eyelid coating. This is why she is scarred and mutilated. Her captors weren't doing out of malevolence or coldness. They did it to ensure SCP-XXXX-1 wouldn't be permanent. All of this would be explained in the interview with her. I didn't talk about it because I was already at 394 words.
  • SCP-XXXX-1 is an event in which peoples reflections return to their natural independent state. This event has a time frame and after a while, the reflections return to reflecting their castors. That's what I meant by resynchronised.

item.title: Re: Slightly confused
item.content:encoded:
That sentence in particular isn't exactly reflective of the Foundationverse's geopolitics. The Foundation is certainly trusted by nations to do its job, but America, Russia, and the UN set up their own organizations since theirs and the Foundation's ideologies aren't the exact same.

In reality, there's a bunch of rivalry and hostility between the Foundation and PENTAGRAM, the GOC, and GRU Division "P" (when they were active). The Foundation can be interpreted as a kind of neutral party here, which America finds to be useful but not totally helpful in furthering their national interests. Similar story for the UN, since their beliefs often place them in opposition to the Foundation, and same with Russia during the Cold War.

In essence, other national groups exist because the nations that sponsor them have specific goals that the Foundation couldn't fulfill, whether that be supremacy on the world stage or the destruction of the anomalous.

item.title: Re: They Just Keep Searching
item.content:encoded:
Thanks so much for the feedback, I really appreciate it regardless of your experience - it's always good to have a fresh pair of eyes on things.

Please let me know if you remember what you think this sounds similar to. I had a search around the wiki before I started seriously considering the idea but the closest things I could find were:
SCP-988 - a wooden box that cannot be opened as all attempts are "conveniently" interrupted, but this is its only anomalous trait.
SCP-216 - the only real similarity with this one is the fact that it's a kind of safe.
SCP-902 - a box that emits a ticking noise people become convinced is counting down. It does compel people to open the box, but it CAN be opened and doesn't appear to contain anything, so I figured it was different enough from this one to be its own thing.

As for the rest, some of those questions I do have answers for but didn't have space to detail them in the initial post due to the word limit. I have written an SCP draft for this idea to help organise my thoughts about it - I won't link it here as it hasn't been specifically asked for but I'll use info from it to answer your questions.

+ show block
– hide block

1: I go into quite a lot of detail about this in the draft. There are exact measurements given for width, length, ceiling height and floor thickness of the SCP's cell to ensure no accidental exposure. A circular hazard warning line is also painted on the floor around the hazardous zone so people can avoid it if they have to go in the cell.

2: The anomalous effect isn't triggered by staring at the safe, it's triggered by spacial proximity. Anyone within 10 m of the safe is affected - you could be affected without even knowing the safe is there initially, and it seems completely unremarkable until roughly the 3 hour mark. Those 3 hours are cumulative so if you were to spend 10 minutes in the hazardous zone each day, you would become infected after roughly 18 days. The discovery report explains that it was found in the basement of a house, with the proximity zone edging out into other parts of the house so the inhabitants were affected over time. Though I may have to increase the zone to 15 or 20 m to make this more believable, so thanks for highlighting that. I did consider making the amount of time much shorter, but then I couldn't think of a conceivable way for Foundation staff to transport the safe without being infected.

3: We don't know - I wanted that to be part of the mystery. The safe appears centuries old (though impossible to properly analyse), but Foundation researchers reportedly argue that if it were as old as it looks it would have been found earlier due to its effects. So it could be an ancient artifact of unknown origin, or something an anomalous entity recently made for a laugh and just made it LOOK old. As I mentioned, it is found in a basement after police investigate due to violence committed by an SCP-XXXX-1 instance who resided there.

4: As above, we don't know for sure. Though it feels unlikely to me that any non-anomalous humans could create it.

5: No, the surface is impenetrable by measuring equipment as well as weapons - all attempts at observing the contents have yielded no results.

6: 280 kg.

7: After the 3 hours of exposure they can transform fully at any time between a few hours and 2 days after the fact. Exact length varies depending on the individual, but none have been less than 2 hours and none have been more than 2 full days.

8: Yes. As previously mentioned, observing the safe is not the hazardous part. As long as you're more than 10 m away you're fine. However, the SCP can affect cameras as all cameras monitoring it spontaneously deactivate during its active episodes.

9: Nobody has yet been harmed by the safe itself. Though the incident report of cameras being deactivated and motion sensors being tripped MAY imply there's an entity inside the safe that can leave and may be harmful, but no harm has been done yet and the safe itself could just be affecting electronics without anything leaving it - I wanted that to be open to interpretation.

Thanks for the questions, and the naming suggestions too! I like "Isolated Safe" quite a lot but I wonder if it's too similar to SCP-216's "The Safe". I will definitely consider all of those suggestions though! :)

item.title: The Spider Queen (First SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not yet.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: haven't settled on one yet

Elevator Pitch: A Euclid-class queen of spiders that was saddened by humanity's cruelty towards her children to the point where her heart literally cracked. Because of this, she's surprisingly passive. She can make new species of spiders (both normal and anomalous) at will, and spiders flock to her.

Narrative Pitch: Though she has waged several wars against humanity in the past due to the mistreatment of her children that got fiercer as time went on, her heart eventually cracked, flushing all hatred from her body in a single moment. All that was left behind was sorrow. Sorrow for her fallen children, and sorrow for sending her children to die in who knows how many wars that they never won. So she packed her things and left the mainland, retreating to an island. Many, many years later, the foundation responds to a radio signal from a battleship claiming that they were being attacked by an enormous spider. It's revealed that she created this spider as a guardian for her personal island that she sends out if she senses that people with bad intentions are coming to her island. The foundation does its thing, making the island as secret as possible while trying to study the spider queen. Eventually, the foundation manages to conduct some interviews with her.

Hook: Aside from the aforementioned interviews, which reveal her backstory, this SCP should be interesting among the other spider-based SCPs that she's not immediately hostile to people. There should also be implications that some of the spider-based SCPs the foundation keeps tabs on are relics of these ancient wars fought by her.

Additional Notes: While she has potential, I want to hear your input for how I could improve her concept.

item.title: Form 1004-E: Proposal for Reclassification
item.content:encoded:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/deathbygin-2

A short tale for my authored article SCP-5118.

Spoiler / Explanation
Minimize

As Dr. Atmos gather information from Dr. Williams, it's implied that SCP-5118 is actually a dog who is a reality bender, turned human, and turned back into a dog when about to be captured. Evidence to support this includes:

  • SCP-5118 did not act like most other reality benders do when discovering they have powers (usually by hiding them from others).
  • SCP-5118 manifests chocolate, grapes, and soda - all things a dog cannot eat.
  • SCP-5118 appeared to be smiling while being chased.
  • SCP-5118 does not attempt to breach containment because it's current living situation is already ideal (it gets a bed, new toys, guaranteed food and water, and socializes with staff daily when they provide it with food).
  • Using it's powers while in containment would risk exposing itself. Since it's implied that it's "original form" is already a dog, the scans / tests from the SCP article would show nothing.

I wanted to write this tale to add a twist to the article without making this the clear-cut canon. Please let me know what you think.

item.title: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
Hey! Not a greenlighter, sorry.

So, your object itself is interesting enough- a nice cultural reference is generally good, and you also changed it up a little so that it wasn't just pulling straight from stories that already exist. Overall, the anomaly is solid enough, so that's good.

Your narrative is interesting. I enjoy the idea of a mysterious location like this one that represents a lot of danger for the Foundation, but if you leave it where you're leaving it now, the ending might be regarded as having too little detail. This seems like something that would be explored more than once, albeit with more appropriate gear the second time (for things like cognitohazards). Or, you could use drone exploration, if that would work. Really, I just think that you should either shine some light on this "festival" or at least provide some insight as to why they're saying "come to the festival." If you intend to leave the reader with a lot of questions, you should get them a little closer to their answers so that they can infer details, rather than leaving it completely vague.

This type of object seems like the kind of thing that the Foundation is going to have a hard time containing- a sort of "neutralize the threat by any means" type of scenario. Do you plan on expanding on that through the narrative? That would definitely involve more exploration logs/action scenarios and stuff along those lines. I recommend including those types of things if that's the storyline you want to use, but if these are easy to contain, then I would instead suggest controlled experiments and research logs. In the end, though, you should do whatever you feel is best for the article and go from there- these are just suggestions.

Overall, the concept looks good. Try to get some additional advice on how to develop this narrative if you feel like you need it. I hope I was able to help. Good luck developing your idea!

Can't give you a green light but I can give you some constructive criticism. This is SCP sounds intriguing but it does kind of sound similar to something else I may have read.
A couple of questions you might ask yourself is

  1. how is the SCP ( the safe) stored or contained?
  2. 3 hours seems a bit long for someone to stare at something, what makes the SCP force people to observe it for 3 hours cumulatively in the first place( ie what makes them come back) ?
  3. what is the origin of the the safe?
  4. Is the safe man made or otherworldly ?
  5. can the safe be x-rayed or anything along those lines to find out what is inside?
  6. How much does it weigh?
  7. How long before victims turn into the sub entities?
  8. Can you observe the safe using a camera at 10m for 3 hours cumulatively without turning into a sub entity?
  9. Can it kill/hurt you without the SCP sub entities?

Im a first time time SCP writer too so I don't know everything.
Here are some free name ideas for your SCP, Isolated Safe, Termination Safe, Safe?, The deviant box, The ?, The box without a key, Denied entry, The metal door to something.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Sharkingdom Studios,

As per the Draft Forum Policies, new authors are to get their concepts reviewed and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers on the Idea Critique Forums before posting on the Draft Critique Forums.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. They can also assist in letting you know if something similar exists on the site already, or inform you of various clichés/pitfalls to be cautious of. These elements are more effectively addressed earlier in the writing process.

If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Drafts Critique
Forum thread: My (First) SCP

On that note, this seems more Apollyon (or at least Keter) than Euclid. Given the amount of plankton and filter-feeding organisms in the ocean, those spores will be being cobbled down like no one's business. A passing whale gulping down a mouthful, a single baitfish swallowing them while snapping at some plankton, a copepod eating one; all will lead to a new instance.

The fungicide spray might reliably prevent it from releasing spores, but that's not mentioned in the article and it had about a week of growth before the Foundation got there, then however long it took the Foundation to figure out what to do before they started spraying the fungicide. And even then, mistakes can happen; it's going to be hard to uniformly apply the fungicide to every nook and cranny of the wreckage and the rig.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
Not a greenlighted but you asked me to review so I shall deliver.

Firstly, I think that the idea of linking the SCP to the poem doesn't feel like it adds much to the story. There isn't much evidence stated saying that this is a definite fact, and it just feels like a thrown in unnecessary detail. You could likely improve this by directly linking the SCP to the author of the play in an addendum log. If you would like to be more subtle about it you could just elaborate on this more on the interview aspect.

Secondly, there doesn't seem to be much information on how the foundation got ahold of or found out about SCP-XXXX. Where was it found, when was it found, and how was it found? Again adding addendum logs can allow you to add this kind of information quite easily.

Lastly, maybe elaborate more on the earlier captors of SCP-XXXX, and maybe add something about how the methods the other foundation used worked. It doesn't have to be something like that, but just elaborating in general would make it better. I know this seems repetitive, but an addendum log would help with this as well if your main worry is that it cant fit into the story well.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that you should elaborate on some of the plotlines, or details or just remove them entirely. You can use addendum logs and interviews to get across these points relatively easily, and I think that this story just needs a bit of freshening up. Other than that it is a great SCP idea, and can become something good if you fill in these holes.

item.title: Re: You left me (scp article)
item.content:encoded:
Hello there! I'll take a look for you.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

First up, the Elevator Pitch. I'm not 100% how to feel about it, and I can't quite put my finger on why. I think it might be because of the whole 'mysterious deaths happen because mystery' feel it gives me. I know there's a thematic reason for this, so I'll touch on that next.

So, this is a weird phenomenon that causes town-wide genocides via grief? I do like that thematically; the idea of dying via depression and missing dead loved ones literally dying of sadness and gried, but I feel a sort of…idk, disconnect? Probably not the word I'm looking for.

Is it a weird compulsion effect? Is it the paranormal influence of an external entity that feeds off the emotion of grief? Is it just a specific phenomenon centralized on some small towns but not others?

I'm having a very difficult time putting this feeling I'm feeling into words.

This phenomenon is brought to the attention of the foundation when a survivor recounts his tale, and it lines up with multiple similar cases.

I thought it wiped out entire towns?

Eventually, they nail down an inconsistent pattern, and are able to prevent the phenomenon from occurring if they catch wine soon enough.

Prevent it how? Evacuate an entire town, wait for the one terminally ill patient to die, then move them all back in? Sounds too time consuming and costly if you ask me.

phenomenon that causes major loss of life over something simple.

I'm on board with the emotion you're going for, but I don't think it's all fleshed out enough yet. You're aiming for the message of not allowing grief to kill you after losing a loved one, but the only thing to show is that everybody dies off in a small town after one person dies beforehand.

Honestly, try thinking of a few characters and put them in this situation and maybe flesh out the anomaly a little more and you'll definitely have something.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day! 👍👍👍👍

item.title: Re: The Aspiring Therapist (First SCP)
item.content:encoded:
I think this is a weird type of X-Men type character, (or X-Child, really, but you get the point.) wherein he is innately beneficial to the Foundation and the story implies that they willingly have him help them.

I'm not really on board with this because 1.) All the crosslinking that would need to be done would be excessive and crosslinking is frowned upon for a first time author.

2.) The Foundation isn't really readily of help from willing SCPs nowadays. For humanoids, they toss them into a containment chamber and give them enough amenities to live and to not die of severe depression.

Though the idea of a kid talking to anomalous objects does interest me, I'm not really sure how well this can be achieved. 'Kid talks to usually non-vocal thing' is…kinda hard to get right. In fact, the only instance I can personally think of is Harry Potter talking to snakes.

If you find a way to portray an interesting narrative of a kid talking to objects, make it believable, and find a way to actually kinda prove it to researchers instead of just trying to convince the researchers to believe it at face value, then you might have something. As of now, though, I'm not on board with this.

item.title: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is that the SCPs are based on Irish fairies, who are (in short) tricksters who manipulate humans in various ways. Whether that be by manipulating their mind to go crazy or manipulating their body to disform them. Fairies were blamed for various things in medieval Ireland, some of those include stuff like schizophrenia or disabilities being 'curses' from fairies. The SCP will differ from generic fairies by being inherently malevolent when the original fairies are not.

Central Narrative: After various missing person reports, and the discovery of a body missing a symmetrical hole in their chest, the Foundation investigate a forest in Ireland. While investigating, one of the team starts hearing voices telling them to kill their teammates and to 'come to the festival' upon telling the team of this the MTF, assuming the SCP has something to do with this, detain and amnestisize the teammate. They leave one MTF to bring the affected teammate out of the forest to safety and continue. After a bit, the MTF see various colorful lights in the distance, and they all begin to hear voices telling them to 'come to the festival'. At this point, the MTF stop broadcasting their video and we are left with only their audio. The captain, who appears to be the least affected, describes what's happening while the others start going mad. Eventually, the captain attempts to flee the situation at which various etheral screaming can be heard before he goes offline.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Well I tried my best to make sure it leaves a lot of questions, and the fact that it's a twist on what is normally considered cute or harmless is pretty interesting.

Additional Notes: I don't know how I feel about the narrative (which is why I'm not seeking a greenlight yet), so I would like critisicm to be focused on that.
